Subject: Capacity playtest: VanguardTech Dedicated burst + autoscale policy

Hi Maya / Jared —

Thanks again for walking through the Dedicated sizing numbers last week. Per our call, VanguardTech's Q3 load test includes two burst windows (batch ingest at ~02:00 UTC and a bursty inference spike around 18:00 UTC). Before we lock final slab sizing I want to run a short playtest to validate the autoscale behavior and eviction characteristics under the exact job mix you plan to run.

Ask: can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow so we can schedule the playtest for Friday?
- Representative job mix (percent of short chat vs long-context batch inference).
- Typical concurrent sessions for the 18:00 spike (peak qps or concurrent sessions).
- Any pinned models or strict version pinning that disallows fallback to smaller variants.

What Redwood will run for the playtest (high level):
- 2-hour simulated spike that reproduces the ingest and inference phases (we'll supply a workload harness).
- A/B autoscale policy tests: (A) conservative scale with lower prewarm and aggressive eviction, (B) aggressive prewarm and permissive eviction.
- KV/prefix cache warmup and cold-start metrics captured for token latency breakdown.
- Failover run: force a regional fallback to test model-variant routing.

I'll loop Karthik on the configuration details and Ben will call out the billing/credit implications. If Friday doesn't work, suggest next Tuesday.

Attachments: sample playtest harness and a checklist (I put stubs in the Drive link).

Best,

Subject: Re: Capacity playtest: VanguardTech Dedicated burst + autoscale policy

Thanks Soojin — quick answers below and attaching a CSV of historical peak windows (last 90 days).

- Job mix: ~75% short-chat (<=128 tokens; median latency sensitivity), ~25% batch long-context (avg 2k tokens).
- 18:00 spike: typically 1.2k concurrent chat sessions, peaking qps ~2.8k for ~18 minutes; the bulk of traffic is fan-out inference (many short requests).
- Model pinning: we must keep the 1.1.0 production model pinned; fallback to a quantized 1.1.q variant is OK provided output checks pass.

We can make the Friday slot work (UTC Fri 02:00 and 18:00 windows both possible). If you need more telemetry, I can also provide sample traces for a representative request.

-Jared

Subject: Re: Capacity playtest: VanguardTech Dedicated burst + autoscale policy

Thanks for the data, Jared — this clarifies a lot. A few technical constraints and the proposed plan from our side: 

Constraints / observations:
- The long-context batch jobs (2k tokens) will dominate GPU memory usage; even with quantized kernels they require longer slot residency and larger KV cache footprint.
- To avoid tail latency regressions, we should not over-commit prewarm to chat-only instances; we want a mix of prewarmed slots sized for the median request and a small pool reserved for heavy batch.
- Eviction policy: recommend time-based LRU with a small protected pool (10-15% of slab) for pinned-models to respect your pinning requirement.

Proposed playtest plan (technical):
1) Baseline run (no prewarm): measure cold-start latency for representative requests.
2) Policy A (conservative): prewarm = 25% of steady-state concurrency, scale cooldown 90s, aggressive eviction after 120s idle.
3) Policy B (aggressive prewarm): prewarm = 50% steady-state, cooldown 30s, permissive eviction 300s idle with KV cache retention.
4) Model-variant fallback run: route 20% of traffic to 1.1.q variant and run regression checks.
5) Failure injection: remove one slab mid-run and observe failover routing and queued request behavior.

I'll synthesize the exact autoscale config (YAML) and share before the run. Also adding a short checklist for the on-call team so ops knows when to step in.

-Karthik

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. A couple of commercial notes before we kick off Friday's playtest: 

- Consumption crediting: because this is a playtest that intentionally drives above-commit bursts, Redwood will apply transient test credits equivalent to 40% of the observed overage tokens for both spike windows (applied to the invoice for May). This is a one-time concession to validate policy.
- If the playtest surfaces a need for a higher shoulder slab or a permanent increase in reserved capacity, we'll issue an SOW addendum and provide a credit schedule for the ramp period (typical 30/60-day cadence).
- DocuSign: attaching a short capacity addendum that documents the test scope and credit terms — please sign and return before the run so finance has the test documented.

If you prefer, we can also scope a repeatable automation that runs a similar sanity test each month tied to your release window.

Thanks — Ben
